rationale: Review the retained logical-deadline case and consolidate it with the main and control receipts. The timeout receipt holds: the wrong-context batch did not complete before the 50-tick deadline, returned RequestTimeout at logical tick 51, and was removed by the GC path. This measures the bounded client endpoint and corrects the main account's prior limitation that the timeout was only source-supported. Separately trace observer ReadIndex admission and response routing to check whether the remote branch is follower-only; the source shows observers use the same leader queue and pending-read path, so the impact scope extends to observer-originated reads even though only follower-originated reads were measured.

knowledge.statement: In the logical-deadline case, after node 2 received the later context's reply and the real ready index was applied, the original read batch remained at index zero and did not complete before the 50-tick deadline. At logical tick 51 the pendingReadIndex GC returned RequestTimeout and removed the batch.
knowledge.conditions: Same three-peer in-process harness and later-first context ordering; a test-only in-memory ILogDB; node 2's request created with a 50-tick timeout; the applied ready index was supplied before the logical clock was advanced to 51; production code unchanged.

knowledge.statement: handleLeaderReadIndex rejects a witness source but does not reject an observer source; it queues the request in the same readIndex path and broadcasts the confirmation heartbeat to voting members. An observer's local ReadIndex is forwarded by handleObserverReadIndex to handleFollowerReadIndex, and its response is routed through handleObserverReadIndexResp to handleFollowerReadIndexResp and the same pendingReadIndex consumer.
knowledge.conditions: The observer has a known leader, the leader has a committed entry in its current term, and the leader accepts the queued request. This is a source trace; observer-originated reads were not executed in the retained receipts.

interpretations.rationale: The current conclusion remains a bounded liveness and client-contract defect for follower-originated ReadIndex requests when a later queued context is confirmed first. The main receipt admits node 2's context {101,1002} at event 0 and node 3's context {202,2003} at event 1; event 2 replies to node 2 with node 3's context and log index 4; event 3 leaves node 2's original batch at index zero after the real ready index 4 was applied; event 4 shows the later context-101 confirmation produces no context-correct reply and no completion. The source cause remains the remote reply construction in handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation using the confirming heartbeat's Hint/HintHigh instead of the queued request's s.ctx, while confirm deletes the earlier queue entry and pendingReadIndex.addReady requires an exact SystemCtx key. The sequential control confirms the same consumer path with node 2's admitted context first: its reply carries that context and completion is 1 with batch index 4. The logical-deadline case keeps the later-first ordering: its event 1 records original_batch_index zero, no completion before the 50-tick deadline, RequestTimeout at advanced tick 51, and the stale batch absent after GC. Together these distinguish a context-association defect from a general consumer or harness failure and measure the bounded client endpoint. The main reply's log index is a later committed index, so no stale-read value or safety violation is established. The request remains uncompleted after a valid applied index until the measured logical timeout. Source admission also shows observers are not excluded from the leader's ReadIndex queue and use the same observer response path; the impact scope therefore includes observer-originated reads, although the retained receipts measured only follower-originated reads.

knowledge.assertion: The confirming context returns earlier queued requests while preserving each request's own SystemCtx.
Remote replies are tagged with the confirming heartbeat context instead of the queued request's context.
A response with a nonmatching SystemCtx leaves the original pending batch at index zero and cannot complete it.
The exercised later-confirmation ordering produced a mismatched reply context and left the earlier read batch unready after the ready index was applied.
The sequential-confirmation control completed when the admitted context was confirmed first.
The logical-deadline case returned RequestTimeout at tick 51 and removed the stale batch.
Observer-originated ReadIndex requests enter the same leader queue and pending-read response path.

counterevidence: The source path that constructs the remote reply uses m.Hint and m.HintHigh; no re-tagging occurs between that send and node 2's consumer in the main probe.
The main reply's log index was 4 and the ready index was 4, so neither the main nor timeout execution shows a stale committed index or stale application state.
The late context-101 confirmation produced zero context-correct replies and completion remained zero.
The sequential control completed with the admitted context, so the main failure is not a general inability of the harness or pending-read consumer to complete.
The timeout receipt shows a client timeout and cleanup, not a successful stale read; it measures the bounded endpoint without establishing a safety violation.
limitations: The ILogDB is test-only and in-memory; disk failure, restart, snapshots, and real transport delay were not exercised.
The main test applies the returned ready index synchronously; the companion timeout receipt measures the logical deadline at tick 51, not wall-clock scheduling.

The exercised scope is a three-voter in-process group with follower-originated reads. Observer-originated reads are source-supported to use the same path but were not measured; other membership layouts were not measured.
The sequential control holds only for its exercised first-context ordering; it does not establish safety or completion for all schedules.
The observed wrong reply context is a correlation defect; it is not by itself evidence that the returned read index is stale or that a wrong data value was read.
interpretations.joint_history: The main, control, and timeout receipts are separate fixed experiments from the same harness family and three-peer in-memory setup. The main experiment withholds node 2's earlier heartbeat and confirms node 3's later context first. The control confirms node 2's admitted context first on the same handlers and pending-read consumer. The timeout experiment repeats the later-first ordering and advances the pending-read logical clock past the caller's 50-tick deadline. The differences are intentional ordering and deadline comparisons; the timeout case does not claim a result under a correct-context reply.
